purpose: turn source into a deterministic, reproducible build that anyone can rerun and get the same result
entry_criteria: Source is in version control with a lockfile
A clean build environment is available
procedure: Pin the toolchain and dependency versions and build in a clean, defined environment.
Build with a single documented command that needs no manual steps or local state.
Stamp the build with the commit id and build number, and avoid embedding timestamps that change the output.
Build twice and compare outputs (checksums) to check reproducibility; investigate differences.
Keep build logs and fail on warnings the team treats as errors.
Hand the output to artifact management (stage 114) with its checksum.
acceptance_criteria: Build runs from a clean checkout with one command
Two builds of the same commit produce identical checksums or differences are explained
validation_method: Rebuild in CI on a clean runner.

validation.command: make build && sha256sum dist/app.tar.gz > /tmp/a.sum && make clean && make build && sha256sum -c /tmp/a.sum   # example

validation.check: read the build log for steps that pull unpinned inputs

failure_modes.mode: Build works only on one machine
failure_modes.detection: CI build fails on a clean runner
failure_modes.response: Move local state into declared inputs

failure_modes.detection: Two builds differ only by time

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Two builds of commit a1b2c3 on clean runners produce the same archive checksum after the team sets a fixed file ordering and strips the build-time field.
